PRENATAL GENETIC TESTING REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Referring Physician: Dr. [redacted name]
Date of Collection: [redacted date]
Date of Report: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Ultrasound abnormalities detected during pregnancy. Screening for chromosomal trisomies (13, 18, 21).

SPECIMEN
Fetal sample obtained via amniocentesis at 32 weeks gestation
Specimen Type: Uncultured amniotic fluid
Specimen ID: [redacted ID]

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR) for rapid aneuploidy detection

METHODOLOGY
QF-PCR analysis was performed on uncultured amniotic fluid cells using fluorescently labeled primers for short tandem repeat (STR) markers specific to chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. Multiple informative markers were analyzed for each chromosome to detect trisomy, monosomy, and triploidy. DNA was extracted using standard protocols and amplified using multiplex PCR. Fragment analysis was performed on an automated genetic analyzer.

RESULTS
Chromosome 13: Normal diallelic pattern observed
Chromosome 18: Normal diallelic pattern observed  
Chromosome 21: Normal diallelic pattern observed

Molecular Karyotype: rsa(13,18,21)×2

INTERPRETATION
No abnormality detected. QF-PCR analysis shows a normal complement for chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. No evidence of trisomy 13 (Patau syndrome), trisomy 18 (Edwards syndrome), or trisomy 21 (Down syndrome) was identified in this fetal sample.

LIMITATIONS
This test is designed to detect whole chromosome aneuploidies of chromosomes 13, 18, and 21 only. It does not detect:
- Structural chromosome abnormalities
- Segmental imbalances or microdeletions/duplications
- Low-level mosaicism (<20%)
- Aneuploidies of other chromosomes
- Single gene disorders
- Maternal cell contamination cannot be completely excluded

RECOMMENDATIONS
Given the ultrasound abnormalities noted, follow-up testing at a genomic laboratory is recommended to investigate other potential genetic causes. Options may include chromosomal microarray analysis or comprehensive genomic testing.

This report has been reviewed and authorized by:
[redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director
